::: {#thm-related-classes}
#### Related elements have the same class

Let $\sim$ be an equivalence relation on a set $S$ (@def-equivalence-relation), and let $a, b \in S$.
Then $a \sim b$ if and only if $[a] = [b]$ (@def-equivalence-class).

:::

::: {.content-hidden when-format="revealjs"}

{{< slidebreak >}}

::: proof

($\Leftarrow$)
Suppose $[a] = [b]$.
Since $\sim$ is reflexive, $a \sim a$, so $a \in [a]$.
So $a \in [b]$, which means $a \sim b$.

($\Rightarrow$)
Suppose $a \sim b$.
We show $[a] = [b]$ by double inclusion (@thm-double-inclusion).

- Let $x \in [a]$, so $x \sim a$.
  Since $a \sim b$ and $\sim$ is transitive, $x \sim b$, so $x \in [b]$.
  So $[a] \subseteq [b]$.
- Let $x \in [b]$, so $x \sim b$.
  Since $\sim$ is symmetric, $a \sim b$ gives $b \sim a$,
  and then transitivity gives $x \sim a$, so $x \in [a]$.
  So $[b] \subseteq [a]$.

:::

:::
